title: Trump Wants to Rebuild a Public Golf Course in Washington
summary:
President Donald Trump wants to rebuild East Potomac Golf Links. It is a public golf course in Washington, D.C., about 2 miles from the White House. It sits on national park land.

On Sunday, Trump wrote online that the course is "old, broken, dilapidated." He said work will start on November 15. The course will close for about 15 months. He shared a plan for a fancy new course that could hold big tournaments.

But there is a court case about it. In February, a group and two people sued the government. They say a fancy course would make it cost more to play. They say the course was meant to be "open to all people."

The government says the people suing have not shown they were harmed. A judge, Ana C. Reyes, told the government to stop cutting down trees at the park. Now the government wants a different judge.

The next court hearing is on Monday.
why_it_matters: Public parks belong to everyone, so changes to them can affect families who use them.
